discussions.name: Boulder
discussions.covers: Front Range, Summit County and the northern mountains
messages: Cloudy and cooler today with areas fog this morning across northeast Colorado.
Scattered rain and mountain snow showers, mainly south of I-70.
A return to mild and dry conditions Sunday through Tuesday.

discussions.name: Grand Junction
discussions.covers: the western and central mountains, Aspen to the San Juans
messages: Valley rain and mountain snow returns to the forecast this weekend favoring the southern mountains and adjacent foothills.
Quiet conditions return briefly Sunday afternoon and Monday before another round of precipitation arrives during the middle of next week.
Unsettled and cool conditions are favored to persist into the late week period as well.

discussions.name: Pueblo
discussions.covers: the southern mountains: Sangre de Cristos, eastern San Juans, Monarch
messages: Upper trough crosses southern Colorado today, with a couple waves of showers/isolated t-storms moving through the area in the afternoon/evening.

Higher mountains, above 8-9k feet, will see snow today, heaviest in the eastern San Juan Mts, where 4-7 inches is expected. Rain/snow mix possible Monument Hill late this evening, though any accumulations here will be minor.
Dry with a slow warning trend Sun-Mon, before another fast moving trough brings snow to the mountains, mainly along the Continental Divide Tue/Wed.

A strong winter storm will move through the Rockies and onto the plains toward next weekend, though much uncertainty remains on the ultimate track of the system and where the greatest impacts/heaviest precip will occur.

report.message:
Welcome to the weekend, Copper Mountain! And with the weekend comes the welcome sight of snowfall!

Today, expect mostly cloudy skies, with snow showers developing around mid-morning and continuing throughout much of the day. Temperatures will hover near freezing, with light winds shifting to the west as the day progresses. Snowfall accumulations of up to a few inches are possible, giving us a nice taste of winter.

And if this storm doesn't deliver quite as much snow as we're hoping for, don't put those snow dances away just yet! Another round of snowfall is in the forecast for the middle of next week, bringing additional opportunities to build our early-season snowpack.

Enjoy the weekend, and we'll see you on the mountain!

Lifts & Terrain: American Eagle will be spinning at 9 AM with access to Rhapsody, Fair Play and Main Vein. Please note: NO green/beginner terrain is currently available.

Woodward Copper: An early-season hike-to park is open at the top of American Eagle.

Uphill Access: Uphill travel is CLOSED at Copper Mountain. Access is expected to open mid-December.

Parking & Transportation: All interior lots are paid parking lots. The Flyer Lot is restricted to parking pass holders only, while the Alpine Lot is free for day skier parking. The Copper Loop and Blue Route buses run starting at 5:30 AM.

Food & beverage: Several restaurants are open for the season, including Sawmill Pizza and Taphouse, Aerie Food Hall, Downhill Dukes, Camp Hale, plus Jack’s Bar & Slopeside Grill.
